solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: to initial a document is to put your name to it
letters are what the mail carries

annotation.surface: A note about the initials that stand in for something, like a label or abbreviation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initial' looks like an adjective describing the letters; here it is a verb, to put your initials on something.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a pointer at a road junction indicates the way to go.

blocks.note: to emphasise a point or a syllable
the strain of pressure and worry

annotation.surface: Someone making a tense emotional state even worse.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses share nothing but spelling: one a verb about emphasis, the other a noun about strain.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses of one word: the verb for emphasising, and the noun for mental strain.

indicators.note: a jacket wraps round what it covers, so the two letters on either side wrap round OVER

blocks.note: the last letter of 'stealing', sitting just before 'over'
the first letter of 'ninety', sitting just after 'over'

annotation.surface: A thief running off with more than ninety jackets.
annotation.walkthrough: An unusual device: the letters touching 'over' in the clue itself, the end of 'stealing' and the start of 'ninety', are the jackets wrapped round it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: running a country or a company means being in charge of it.

entries.clue: Move to the hard shoulder in Jersey (8)

blocks.note: what a driver does to stop at the roadside, as a two-word phrase
a knitted top, not the Channel Island

annotation.surface: A driver stopping on the motorway verge on the island of Jersey.
annotation.walkthrough: The hard shoulder is the British name for the emergency lane beside a motorway. The capital J makes Jersey look like the Channel Island; it is the knitted top.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb read as one word: stopping at the roadside, and a knitted top pulled on over the head.

blocks.note: to cast off, as a tree drops leaves

annotation.surface: Getting rid of a flimsy building.
annotation.walkthrough: A verb and a noun that happen to share a spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: casting something off, and a basic wooden outbuilding.

entries.clue: Something remarkable, nearly the right number? (3-3)

blocks.note: a count that misses by a single unit

annotation.surface: A remarkable result that came within a whisker of the correct figure.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical, hence the question mark: read the answer literally, as a count out by one.
annotation.definitionFit: A unique event is remarkable because it will not happen again.

blocks.note: to spot or become aware of
water that has melted is no longer frozen, read as two words

annotation.surface: Spotting whether a sample is purely meltwater.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful description: split the answer as NOT ICE, which is all that melt-water is.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to detect something is to become aware of it.

entries.clue: Travelling across terrain, more than fifty additionally (8)

annotation.surface: A journey across country of more than fifty miles, on top of everything else.
annotation.walkthrough: Three plain synonyms laid end to end; 'more than fifty' reads as one quantity but splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a journey by land rather than by sea or air crosses terrain.

entries.clue: Hungry rogue fed mash, one getting stuck in (8)

indicators.note: a rogue behaves out of line, so the letters stray from their order
to get stuck in is to be lodged inside, so the I sits within the other letters

annotation.surface: A starving villain given mashed potato, with someone tucking in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting stuck in' is British slang for tucking in eagerly, which suits a hungry rogue; here it places the I inside the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: being starving is being very hungry.

blocks.note: something that goes bang: a handgun
a Catherine wheel is a firework that spins, so it turns round and round

annotation.surface: Choosing fireworks: a banger or a Catherine wheel.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves pretend to be fireworks: a banger is a loud firecracker (and British slang for a sausage), a Catherine wheel a spinning one. Only the second is really a firework; the banger is a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: A whimsical definition by action: a gun makes a bang; and a definition by example, since a spinning firework turns.

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for power goes around R

blocks.note: as in steam power, what drives an engine

annotation.surface: Flower power, the hippy slogan, is roughly right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower power' is a 1960s hippy slogan, so 'Flower' reads as a bloom; it is something that flows.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a flower is a thing that flows, as a river or brook does.

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: trauma = agony, which loses its Y

annotation.surface: The trauma of the festive season.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. A figure here is a shape, not a number or a person; the question mark admits that Christmas only stands for its month.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a ten-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

entries.clue: Saturday evening reserved initially, day for talk (6)

indicators.note: at first, so take the first letter of each word

annotation.surface: Someone keeping Saturday evening free and a set day for a talk.
annotation.walkthrough: Saturday is a teasing choice, since this kind of talk belongs to Sunday; any day will do, and the abbreviation wanted is Monday's.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a preacher's address in church is a kind of talk.

entries.clue: Cryptic clues written by that lady’s hero (8)

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the letters of CLUES are jumbled
written beside, so the jumbled word sits next to the pronoun

blocks.note: the possessive pronoun for a woman

annotation.surface: A woman who writes cryptic clues and her hero.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic clues' reads as crossword talk about the puzzle itself; 'cryptic' is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the strongman of Greek and Roman myth is the classic hero.

entries.clue: Huge figure in invoice arrived, and nothing to invest (7)

indicators.note: to invest is to put money into, so the nothing is put into the word for arrived

blocks.note: the train is in = has arrived

annotation.surface: A huge sum on an invoice, and no money to invest.
annotation.walkthrough: The money words are the disguise: 'nothing to invest' sounds like being broke, but it is a letter going inside another word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a thousand million is a very large number.

indicators.note: ground as in ground up, crushed and re-formed

annotation.surface: Putting something in the earth to attract a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as soil; it is the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the big-billed waterbird is a bird.

indicators.note: soaked up inside, so the answer lies within the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of businesswoman runs into the start of terrific

annotation.surface: A businesswoman absorbed in her investment, which is going terrifically.
annotation.walkthrough: The stake is a poker stake, put in before the deal.
annotation.definitionFit: A gambling term: the stake each player puts into the pot before cards are dealt.

entries.clue: Mislead someone in court, one attempting to deceive … (8)

blocks.note: a member of the jury sits in court

annotation.surface: Misleading someone in court, as a fraudster would.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 18 down, where the same performer produces a rabbit.
annotation.definitionFit: A stage magician's whole act is deception, fooling the audience's eyes.

entries.clue: … whose producing of rabbit is a sporting achievement! (3,5)

annotation.definitionNote: the first definition runs on from 17 down: the magician whose producing of a rabbit is his signature trick

blocks.note: pulling a rabbit from a top hat is the classic stage illusion
three goals or wickets by one player

annotation.surface: A conjuror's rabbit trick is hailed like a sports feat.
annotation.walkthrough: In sport the phrase means three goals by one player in a football match, or three wickets with successive balls in cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: The literal sense, an illusion done with a hat, and the idiom for three successes in one game.

entries.clue: Consignment found in food shop, remarkably (8)

annotation.surface: A shipment turning up in a food shop, surprisingly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' looks like an anagram indicator, but no fodder fits; it is just a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a batch of goods sent out is a consignment.

entries.clue: Stone circle in front of companion (4)

annotation.surface: A stone circle standing before a companion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stone circle' reads as one thing, like Stonehenge; split it after 'Stone'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the iridescent gem is a precious stone.

blocks.note: an informal word for a blunder
a kind of crusty white loaf

annotation.surface: A mistake made in baking.
annotation.walkthrough: The loaf is a British one, long with diagonal slashes across the top.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: informal British for a howler, and a named style of loaf.

blocks.note: baby = small, as in baby carrots
a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A baby put to work for a subordinate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Baby' looks like a noun, an infant; it is the adjective meaning small.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a servile follower is an underling.

indicators.note: done terribly means done badly, so the three letters come out mangled

blocks.note: a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig

annotation.surface: Machinery overheating badly, no doubt about it.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is British informal agreement, like 'OK, sure'.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: the chirpy British way of saying yes, certainly.

entries.clue: Nag in street tethered by aristocrat (6)

indicators.note: held fast by, so the street is held inside the noble

annotation.surface: A horse in the street, tied up by a nobleman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nag' pretends to be a horse, which suits tethering; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to badger someone repeatedly is to nag.

indicators.note: placed in, so the word for thus goes inside the metal

annotation.surface: Scrap placed in a black metal container.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black metal' reads as a unit, even a music genre; it splits into two separate words, with the second one opened up.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to throw overboard or discard is to scrap.

indicators.note: squeezed in means crammed inside, so IN is pressed into the hole

blocks.note: a seedy dump or hole; the 's is 'has'

annotation.surface: A sacred hole, packed tight.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has': the hole has the word squeezed inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: of or from God means holy.

blocks.note: the partner in a double act who sets up the comic

annotation.surface: Beating an honest man.
annotation.walkthrough: A straight man is the member of a comedy double act who plays it serious; 'straight' has nothing to do with honesty here.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: thwarting a plot, and a character whose contrast sets another off.

indicators.note: the apostrophe replacing a final G shows the synonym should drop its G too

blocks.note: increasing = raising, clipped of its last letter as the apostrophe shows

annotation.surface: Fruit getting bigger, said casually.
annotation.walkthrough: The clipped 'increasin'' tells you to clip the synonym the same way.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a dried grape is a fruit.

indicators.note: adapted means changed to fit a new form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A mild television show that has been adapted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A little tame' reads as one description of the show; the definition ends before 'tame'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to some degree means a little.

entries.clue: Relatives in newspaper clearing things up (6)

indicators.note: the relatives are placed in the newspaper, inside its letters

blocks.note: a disparaging word for a low-quality newspaper

annotation.surface: A newspaper clearing up family matters.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a paper setting the record straight; the clearing up is done with a garden tool.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by action: drawing a toothed tool over leaves or debris clears them up.

entries.clue: Doctor early with op, gentleman’s head bandaged – one heading for theatre? (8)

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
a head is the top of something, so the first letter of gentleman is used
bandaged means bound up together, so G is wrapped in with the other letters

annotation.surface: A hospital scene: an early operation, a man's head bandaged, and a trip to theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word evokes a hospital, where 'theatre' means the operating theatre; the answer is off to see a play.
annotation.definitionFit: A whimsical definition by action: someone off to watch a play is heading for the theatre.
